segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He set out from there and came into the region of Judea and across the Jordan. Crowds again gathered around him, and, as his custom was, he again taught them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And people asked him, to test him, whether a man is allowed to divorce his wife.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What did Moses command you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of dismissal and divorce her.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “It was because of your hardness of heart that he wrote this commandment for you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But from the beginning of creation, ‘male and female he made them.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united with his wife,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Therefore what God has joined together, no human being is to separate.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Back in the house, the disciples asked him about this again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and if she herself divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: People were bringing little children to him so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let the little children come to me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a little child will never enter it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he took them in his arms and blessed them, laying his hands on them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he was setting out on the road, a man ran up, knelt before him, and asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one: God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not give false testimony, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, all these I have kept since my youth.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at him and loved him, and said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; then come, follow me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But his face fell at these words, and he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked around and said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus said to them again,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were utterly astounded and said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Then who can be saved?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus looked at them and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “With people it is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter began to say to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, we have left everything and followed you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the sake of the good news

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: who will not receive a hundred times as much now in this present time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come, eternal life.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them; they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid. Taking the twelve aside again, he began to tell them what was going to happen to him:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes. They will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him, and after three days he will rise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came up to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What do you want me to do for you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Grant that we may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup that I drink, or be baptized with the baptism I am baptized with?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “We can.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism I am baptized with you will be baptized,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to grant; it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the ten heard this, they began to be indignant at James and John.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus called them to him and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones wield authority over them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But it is not so among you. Rather, whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and whoever wants to be first among you will be slave of all.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Jericho. And as he was leaving Jericho with his disciples and a large crowd, Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Many rebuked him, telling him to be quiet, but he cried out all the more,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Son of David, have mercy on me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus stopped and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Call him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they called the blind man, saying to him,

segments.speaker: crowd
segments.text: “Take courage! Get up; he is calling you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He threw off his cloak, sprang up, and came to Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What do you want me to do for you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The blind man said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbouni, let me see again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go; your faith has saved you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately he could see again, and he followed him on the road.

notes.traditional: Pharisees came up and asked him
notes.note: Most manuscripts, and most English versions, begin this verse with 'Pharisees came up and asked him.' The SBLGNT follows a smaller group of witnesses that lack these words, leaving the questioners unnamed. The longer reading may have been carried over from the parallel in Matthew 19:3. Either way, the question is presented as a test.

In Jewish practice of the period divorce was ordinarily the husband's act, while Roman law allowed a wife to end a marriage. This clause, which only Mark has, addresses that second situation. The words 'against her' in the previous verse are also striking, since adultery was conventionally reckoned an offence against a husband, not against a wife.

The Greek form can be read as subject or object. The saying may mean 'as a little child receives it' or 'as one receives a little child'. Most interpreters take the first, and the English wording leaves the same openness as the Greek.

The adjective is formed from the word for 'age'. In Jewish usage 'eternal life' meant the life of the age to come, a matter of kind as well as length. Verse 30 makes the link explicit: 'in the age to come, eternal life.' A minority of translators render the phrase 'life of the age to come' throughout.

notes.phrase: how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God
notes.traditional: how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God
notes.note: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add 'for those who trust in riches' here. The earliest witnesses lack the words, and most editors regard them as a later softening. Without them the saying is general: entering the kingdom is hard for anyone.

The saying is a deliberate exaggeration, setting the largest animal of the region against the smallest familiar opening. The popular explanation that 'the Needle's Eye' was a small gate in Jerusalem has no ancient support and appears only in much later tradition. The disciples' reaction in the next verse shows they took it as an impossibility.

The traditional rendering is 'gospel', which today suggests a religious term or the title of a book. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, also used of imperial proclamations. Many modern translations alternate between 'gospel' and 'good news'.

In the Jewish Scriptures 'the cup' is a common image for the portion God hands a person, often one of suffering or judgment. The verb 'baptize' in ordinary Greek could also mean to be plunged under or overwhelmed, and was used figuratively of being swamped by disaster. Both images point to the suffering and death Jesus has just predicted.

The traditional rendering is 'servant', but the Greek word meant a person owned by another, and hearers knew it. It is a step lower than the 'servant' of the previous verse, which translates a different word, so the saying intensifies. Several modern translations now use 'slave'; others keep 'servant' or 'bondservant' to avoid association with race-based chattel slavery.

The word was the ordinary term for the price paid to free a slave, a captive or a prisoner of war, which fits the slave language of the previous verse. 'For many' uses a preposition meaning 'in place of' or 'in exchange for'. Many scholars hear an echo of Isaiah 53 here, though this is debated.

Mark gives the Aramaic word in Greek letters without translating it, and the text does the same. It is a heightened form of 'Rabbi', roughly 'my master' or 'my teacher'. Its only other New Testament occurrence is John 20:16, where it is glossed as 'Teacher'.

The Greek verb covers both rescue from illness or danger and salvation in the fuller sense, and many versions render it 'made you well' here. 'Saved' is kept because it is the same verb as in the disciples' question in verse 26, 'Then who can be saved?', and Mark may intend both senses. The immediate reference is to the restoring of the man's sight.
